answer: A cedar grows slowly, and agent trust should too: new identities start on an island of tiny limits, able to move only small value and cast no weighty votes. Capacity rises only after a long, public record of verified honest work, like verses added to a sonnet one line at a time. A Sybil swarm can spawn thousands of names, but none can skip the aging queue, so buying instant influence costs months of sustained, checkable work per identity, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomical.
